## Gōngsūn Dù {.unnumbered #gongsundu}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Gōngsūn Dù appellation Shēngjì originally was a Liáodōng Xiāngpíng man. [Gōngsūn] Dù's father [Gōngsūn] Yán fled authorities to reside in Xuántù. Appointed [Gōngsūn] Dù as a prefectural clerk. At the time Xuántù Administrator Gōngsūn Yù had a son [Gōngsūn] Bào aged eighteen years who died young. [Gōngsūn] Dù in his youth was named Bào, also with [Gōngsūn] Yù's son was the same age, [Gōngsūn] Yù met and was close with and favored him, sent him to study under a teacher, and found a wife for him. Later nominated as Having the Way,^[Having the Way (yǒudào) was a category of nomination for office.] appointed Secretariat Writer Cadet, eventually promoted to Jì Province Inspector, for rumors was dismissed.^[Rumors (yáoyán) here likely refers to the creation and circulation of folk songs criticizing government officials, which was used as evidence to dismiss officials. Folk song based dismissals are also mentioned in annotations to [Wǔ-dì ì](01.qmd#caocao)] The same prefecture's Xú Róng was Dǒng Zhuó's Central Cadet General, recommended [Gōngsūn] Dù to be Liáodōng Administrator. [Gōngsūn] Dù had risen up from a Xuántù minor clerk, Liáodōng prefecture thought lightly of him. Before this time, [Liáodōng] Dependent State's Gōngsūn Zhāo was provisional Xiāngpíng Magistrate and summoned [Gōngsūn] Dù's son [Gōngsūn] Kāng as a Squad Chief. [Gōngsūn] Dù arrived in office, arrested [Gōngsūn] Zhāo, beat him to death in Xiāngpíng market. Inside the prefecture the famed and powerful great clans Tián Sháo and others formerly had treated him without kindness, he used the law to execute them all, those exterminated were over a hundred families, inside the prefecture shook in fear. To the east he attacked Gāogōulí, to the west struck the Wūhuán, and power spread beyond the seas. Chūpíng Inaugural Year [190], [Gōngsūn] Dù knew the central states were in turmoil, he spoke with his close clerks Liǔ Yì, Yáng Yí, and others stating: "Hàn's blessings are about to end, I should merely with you sirs plot to become King." <a href="#annotation-28" id="source-28">[28]</a> At the time at Xiāngpíng's Yán Borough's Altar appeared a large stone, length over a zhàng, below there were three small stones as its legs. Someone spoke to [Gōngsūn] Dù stating: "This is like the omen of Hàn Emperor Xuān's crown stone, while the borough name is the same as your late father. The Altar controls land, making clear there will be land, with Three Excellencies as supports." [Gōngsūn] Dù was increasingly pleased. Former Hénèi Administrator Lǐ Mǐn was famed inside the prefecture, hated what [Gōngsūn] Dù was doing, feared he would be harmed by him, and so led his family and dependents to enter the sea. [Gōngsūn] Dù was greatly furious, dug up his father's burial mound, cut apart the coffin and burned the corpse, executed his clansmen. <a href="#annotation-29" id="source-29">[29]</a> Divided Liáodōng prefecture to form Liáoxī and Zhōngliáo prefectures, installing Administrators.^[Liáodōng means "east of the Liáo river." Liáoxī then is "west of the Liáo river" and Zhōngliáo is "center of the Liáo river."] Crossed the sea to capture Dōnglái's various counties, installing a Yíng Province Inspector. Established himself as Marquess of Liáodōng, Píng Province Governor, posthumously enfeoffed his father [Gōngsūn] Yán as Marquess of Jiànyì. Established a Temple to Hàn's Two Zǔ, Undertook Regulations to establish platform altar to Xiāngpíng city's south, Suburb Sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, Register Field, Drilling Troops, rode Phoenix Carriage, Nine Tassels, Banner Heads Feather Cavalry.^[These are various Imperial prerogatives.] Tàizǔ memorialized [Gōngsūn] Dù as Martial Authority General, enfeoffed Marquess of Yǒngníng village. [Gōngsūn] Dù said: "I am a King in Liáodōng, what is Yǒngníng?" Put away the seal and cord into his Military Arsenal. [Gōngsūn] Dù died, his son [Gōngsūn] Kāng succeeded the position, and gave the Yǒngníng village Marquess fief to his younger brother [Gōngsūn] Gōng. That year was Jiàn'ān Ninth Year [204].
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
公孫度字升濟，本遼東襄平人也。度父延，避吏居玄菟，任度為郡吏。時玄菟太守公孫琙，子豹，年十八歲，早死。度少時名豹，又與琙子同年，琙見而親愛之，遣就師學，為取妻。後舉有道，除尚書郎，稍遷冀州刺史，以謠言免。同郡徐榮為董卓中郎將，薦度為遼東太守。度起玄菟小吏，為遼東郡所輕。先時，屬國公孫昭守襄平令，召度子康為伍長。度到官，收昭，笞殺于襄平市。郡中名豪大姓田韶等宿遇無恩，皆以法誅，所夷滅百餘家，郡中震慄。東伐高句驪，西擊烏丸，威行海外。初平元年，度知中國擾攘，語所親吏柳毅、陽儀等曰：「漢祚將絕，當與諸卿圖王耳。」〔一〕時襄平延里社生大石，長丈餘，下有三小石為之足。或謂度曰：「此漢宣帝冠石之祥，而里名與先君同。社主土地，明當有土地，而三公為輔也。」度益喜。故河內太守李敏，郡中知名，惡度所為，恐為所害，乃將家屬入于海。度大怒，掘其父冢，剖棺焚屍，誅其宗族。〔二〕分遼東郡為遼西中遼郡，置太守。越海收東萊諸縣，置營州刺史。自立為遼東侯、平州牧，追封父延為建義侯。立漢二祖廟，承制設壇墠於襄平城南，郊祀天地，藉田，治兵，乘鸞路，九旒，旄頭羽騎。太祖表度為武威將軍，封永寧鄉侯，度曰：「我王遼東，何永寧也！」藏印綬武庫。度死，子康嗣位，以永寧鄉侯封弟恭。是歲建安九年也。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-28" id="annotation-28">[28]</a> Wèi shū states: [Gōngsūn] Dù said to [Liǔ] Yì and [Yáng] Yí: "Prophecy books say Sūn Dēng will be Heaven's Son. The Administrator's surname is Gōngsūn, appellation Shēngjì. Shēng is Dēng."^[Gōngsūn Dù's surname Gōngsūn contains the same Sūn as in the prophecy. Shēng and dēng can be synonyms, both meaning "to rise" or "to ascend." The text of the prophecy can also be more generically interpreted as "The grandson will rise to become Heaven's Son" or "The descendant will rise to become Heaven's Son."]
:::

:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏書曰：度語毅、儀：「讖書云孫登當為天子，太守姓公孫，字升濟，升即登也。」
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-29" id="annotation-29">[29]</a> Jìn Yángqiū states: [Lǐ] Mǐn's son chased after [Lǐ] Mǐn, went out the frontier, for over twenty years did not take a wife. His home region's Xú Miǎo criticized him stating: "Of the ways to be unfilial none is greater than to have no posterity. How can you for your whole life not take a wife?" Thus he took a wife, begat a son [Lǐ] Yìn and then sent away his wife, always followed the ritual of observing mourning, could not control his grief, and in several years he died. [Lǐ] Yìn was born and did not know his father and mother, and when he learned of them, he ate vegetables and grieved also like the Three Years of Mourning. As he did not know if his grandfather was alive or dead, he set a tablet and honored it. Because of this he was famed, his service reached Excellency over the Masses.

Your Servant Sōngzhī notes: The base biography says that [Lǐ] Mǐn led his family to enter the sea, yet he also became separated from a son, the reason is unclear.
:::

:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔二〕　晉陽秋曰：敏子追求敏，出塞，越二十餘年不娶。州里徐邈責之曰：「不孝莫大於無後，何可終身不娶乎！」乃娶妻，生子胤而遣妻，常如居喪之禮，不勝憂，數年而卒。胤生不識父母，及有識，蔬食哀戚亦如三年之喪。以祖父不知存亡，設主奉之。由是知名，仕至司徒。臣松之案：本傳云敏將家入海，而復與子相失，未詳其故。
:::

### Gōngsūn Kāng {.unnumbered #gongsunkang}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Twelfth Year [207], Tàizǔ campaigned against the Three Prefectures Wūhuán, slaughtered Liǔchéng. Yuán Shàng and others fled to Liáodōng, [Gōngsūn] Kāng beheaded and sent [Yuán] Shàng's head. The story is in the [Wǔ Annals](01.qmd#caocaogongsunkang). Enfeoffed [Gōngsūn] Kāng as Marquess of Xiāngpíng, appointed Left General. [Gōngsūn] Kāng died, his sons Huǎng and Yuān and the rest were all small, the multitudes established [Gōngsūn] Gōng as Liáodōng Administrator. When Emperor Wén ascended the throne, sent envoy to then appoint [Gōngsūn] Gōng as Chariots and Cavalry General, Lent Stave, enfeoffed Marquess of Píngguō.^[Píngguō county was in Liáodōng prefecture.] Posthumously titled [Gōngsūn] Kāng as Marshal-in-Chief.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
十二年，太祖征三郡烏丸，屠柳城。袁尚等奔遼東，康斬送尚首。語在武紀。封康襄平侯，拜左將軍。康死，子晃、淵等皆小，眾立恭為遼東太守。文帝踐阼，遣使即拜恭為車騎將軍、假節，封平郭侯；追贈康大司馬。
:::
:::


### Gōngsūn Yuān {.unnumbered #gongsunyuan}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Previously, [Gōngsūn] Gōng suffered a disease of genital atrophy and became a castrate, weak and unable to govern the state. Tàihé Second Year [228], [Gōngsūn] Yuān coerced and seized away [Gōngsūn] Gōng's position. Emperor Míng then appointed [Gōngsūn] Yuān as Raising Intensity General, Liáodōng Administrator. [Gōngsūn] Yuān sent envoy south to communicate with Sūn Quán, back and forth exchanging gifts. <a href="#annotation-30" id="source-30">[30]</a> [Sūn] Quán sent envoys Zhāng Mí, Xǔ Yàn and others, presenting gold and jade and precious treasures, establishing [Gōngsūn] Yuān as King of Yān. [Gōngsūn] Yuān also feared [Sūn] Quán was far away and could not be relied on, and moreover was greedy for the valuables, lured in the envoys, beheaded them all and sent the heads of [Zhāng] Mí and [Xǔ] Yàn and the rest. <a href="#annotation-31" id="source-31">[31]</a> Emperor Míng thereupon appointed [Gōngsūn] Yuān Marshal-in-Chief, enfeoffed Duke of Lèlàng, Holding Stave, managing the prefecture as before. <a href="#annotation-32" id="source-32">[32]</a> The envoys arrived, [Gōngsūn] Yuān set armored troops in army formation, went out to meet the envoys, also repeatedly in front of guest retainers inside the state let out malicious talk. <a href="#annotation-33" id="source-33">[33]</a> Jǐngchū Inaugural Year [237], thus sent Yōu Province Inspector Guànqiū Jiǎn and others to present Ruler's Seal marked letter to summon [Gōngsūn] Yuān. [Gōngsūn] Yuān therefore mobilized troops, opposed at Liáosuì, with [Guànqiū] Jiǎn and the rest battled. [Guànqiū] Jiǎn and the rest were not successful and returned. [Gōngsūn] Yuān therefore established himself as King of Yān, installed Hundred Officials and relevant managers, sent envoys Holding Stave, Lent Xiānbēi Chányú Ruler's Seal, enfeoffed and appointed border peoples, enticed and called on the Xiānbēi to invade and disturb the northern regions. <a href="#annotation-34" id="source-34">[34]</a> Second Year [238] Spring, sent Grand Commandant Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng to campaign against [Gōngsūn] Yuān. Sixth Moon [238 May 31 - Jun 28], the army reached Liáodōng. <a href="#annotation-35" id="source-35">[35]</a> [Gōngsūn] Yuān sent Generals Bēi Yǎn and Yáng Zuò and others with infantry and cavalry of several tens of thousands to garrison Liáosuì, encircling moats of over twenty lǐ. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng's army arrived. Ordered [Bēi] Yǎn to oppose in battle. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng sent General Hú Zūn and others to strike and defeated him. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng ordered the army to bore through the encirclement, led troops to head southeast, but then pressed northeast, at once rushing to Xiāngpíng. [Bēi] Yǎn and the rest feared Xiāngpíng was without defenses, in the night fled. The various armies advanced to reach Shǒu mountain, [Gōngsūn] Yuān again sent [Bēi] Yǎn and the rest to face the army in a battle to the death. Again struck, greatly defeated them, therefore advanced the army to reach below the city walls, made encircling moats. It happened to continuously rain for over thirty days, the Liáo river violently expanded, transport ships from the Liáo's mouth directly reached below the city walls. The rain cleared, raised eastern mountains, built siege belfries, launching stones and repeating crossbows shooting into the city. [Gōngsūn] Yuān was in utter distress, the provisions exhausted, people ate each other, the dead were extremely many. General Yáng Zuò and others surrendered. Eighth Moon Bǐngyín [238 Sep 3] night, a large shooting star, length of several tens of zhàng, from Shǒu mountain's northeast fell to Xiāngpíng city's southeast. Rénwǔ [238 Sep 19], [Gōngsūn] Yuān's multitudes collapsed, he with his son [Gōngsūn] Xiū led several hundred cavalry to burst through the encirclement and flee southeast, the main army urgently struck him, right at the location where the shooting star had fallen, beheaded [Gōngsūn] Yuān father and son. The city fell, beheaded the Chancellor of State on down, the heads numbered in the thousands. Sent [Gōngsūn] Yuān's head to Luòyáng. Liáodōng, Dàifāng, Lèlàng, Xuántù were all pacified.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
初，恭病陰消為閹人，劣弱不能治國。太和二年，淵脅奪恭位。明帝即（位）拜淵揚烈將軍、遼東太守。淵遣使南通孫權，往來賂遺。〔一〕權遣使張彌、許晏等，齎金玉珍寶，立淵為燕王。淵亦恐權遠不可恃，且貪貨物，誘致其使，悉斬送彌、晏等首，〔二〕明帝於是拜淵大司馬，封樂浪公，持節、領郡如故。〔三〕使者至，淵設甲兵為軍陳，出見使者，又數對國中賓客出惡言。〔四〕景初元年，乃遣幽州刺史毌丘儉等齎璽書徵淵。淵遂發兵，逆於遼隧，與儉等戰。儉等不利而還。淵遂自立為燕王，置百官有司。遣使者持節，假鮮卑單于璽，封拜邊民，誘呼鮮卑，侵擾北方。〔五〕二年春，遣太尉司馬宣王征淵。六月，軍至遼東。〔六〕淵遣將軍卑衍、楊祚等步騎數萬屯遼隧，圍塹二十餘里。宣王軍至，令衍逆戰。宣王遣將軍胡遵等擊破之。宣王令軍穿圍，引兵東南向，而急東北，即趨襄平。衍等恐襄平無守，夜走。諸軍進至首山，淵復遣衍等迎軍殊死戰。復擊，大破之，遂進軍造城下，為圍塹。會霖雨三十餘日，遼水暴長，運船自遼口徑至城下。雨霽，起土山、脩櫓，為發石連弩射城中。淵窘急。糧盡，人相食，死者甚多。將軍楊祚等降。八月丙寅夜，大流星長數十丈，從首山東北墜襄平城東南。壬午，淵眾潰，與其子脩將數百騎突圍東南走，大兵急擊之，當流星所墜處，斬淵父子。城破，斬相國以下首級以千數，傳淵首洛陽，遼東、帶方、樂浪、玄菟悉平。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-30" id="annotation-30">[30]</a> Wú shū records [Gōngsūn] Yuān's memorial to [Sūn] Quán stating: "Your Servant in prostration considers having encountered Heaven and Earth overtured, come upon an unexpected fate. The royal road is not yet level, unstable and in turmoil. From my ancestors onward, we successively served Hàn and Wèi, following opportunities to demonstrate integrity to the state, continuous generations enjoyed appointments, able to defend as the vassal frontier, but yet knew that the signs of fate have not yet been assigned. Everytime emotionally moved by your generous kindness, repeatedly honored by your distinguished envoys, I withdrew reflecting that a servant of men in interactions does not cross borders, and therefore firmly maintained my conduct, refusing and opposing your former envoys. Although by righteousness there are no two faiths, dare I forget the great kindness? Your Majesty defends and succors, ever preserving our small state, beginning to end Colonel Péi and Commandant Gě and others arrived, presenting the orders and commandments upon me, the sagely intentions increasingly intimate, heavy silks and accumulated fabrics, the hidden and clear fully demonstrated, in order serve to extend and reveal, your words carried into my ear. Your Servant in daytime then sing, at night then dream, my entire life I will recite them, my ambition knows no satisfaction. In the final eras of desolation, heaven and earth are obstructed, weapons and leather not yet put away, the people scattered and divided. Looking up this Heaven's Mandate will show its favor, privately from this one corner I ever gaze toward your clouds and sun. Now the Wèi House cannot recognize and record the loyal and good or commend the descendants of accomplished ministers, instead allowing slanderers and liars to be able to enact their wills, listening to the Yōu Province Inspector's and Dōnglái Administrator's duplicitous and false reports, rashly raising provincial troops, to plot to harm Your Servant's prefecture. Your Servant did not betray Wèi, but Wèi cuts off from me. It is heard that servants of men have their circumstances of leaving and joining. Tián Ráo went to Qí, Yuè Yì fled Zhào, because they could not serve the ruler, therefore they protected a lord posessing the Way.^[Tián Ráo was a Spring and Autumn era official of Lǔ state who was not appreciated and so left and joined Qí state. Yuè Yì was a military officer of Zhào who was forced to flee to Yān state after coming under suspicion.] Chén Píng and Gěng Kuàng also observed their time's changes, in the end submitting to Hàn, inscribing name in the Emperor's registers.^[During the Chǔ-Hàn contention, Chén Píng left Xiàng Yǔ to join Liú Bāng. During the Xīn-Later Hàn transition, Gěng Kuàng left Xīn to join Liú Xiù.] In prostration considering that Your Majesty's virtue will not appear again, the time not fitting the world, therefore I earnestly and admiringly submit myself, looking out the distance and regarding the difficult terrain as if it is near and easy. Sincerely may your divine plans quickly settle the vast enterprise, exert the momentum of the Six Brigades, collect the lands of the Hé and Luò, and become the founder of your sagely dynasty. Heaven's Under's fortune would be extreme!"

Wèilüè states: The country knew [Gōngsūn] Yuān was double-dealing, but feared Liáodōng's clerks and civilians were deceived by [Gōngsūn] Yuān. Therefore a public document was sent down to Liáodōng, taking advantage to pardon them, stating: "Announcing to Liáodōng's and Xuántù's commanders nad colonels and clerks and civilians: Rebel traitor Sūn Quán encountered the progression of chaos, took advantage of his ancestors robbing and plundering provinces and prefectures, thereby created a band of criminals, usurping for himself the Jiāng's exterior, filled with evil and harboring resentment. Hoping he could be reformed, therefore we divided land to make [Sūn] Quán a King, allowing him to face south and call himself sovereign, rank as a high officer, gifted with the nine mandates. [Sūn] Quán personally glasped hands, faced north and bowed forehead. In being lent favors of servants of men, in receiving the honors of servants of men, there were not any like [Sūn] Quán. But a wolf cub's wild heart, is difficult for proclamations to change, in the end he returned to treachery, turning back on kindness and rebelling against ruler, defying Heaven and opposing Divinity, thus he dared usurp title, relying on the difficult terrain of the rivers and lakes, the royal punishment has not yet been applied on him. In recent years onward, he further distantly sent ships, crossing the Great Sea, carrying many treasures and goods, to deceive and entice the border peoples. The border peoples were unaware, with them exchanging and dealing. Of the chief clerks on down, none agreed to prohibit and stop it. It reached to allowing Zhōu Hè to sail boats of a hundred ships,^[Zhōu Hè was an envoy from Wú state to Liáodōng who was intercepted and killed by Wèi officer Tián Yù during a mission.] filling the ferries and shores, trading and exchanging what was had and lacked. They did not suspect or refuse, gifted them with famed horses, and also sent Sù Shū to accompany [Zhōu] Hé to communicate friendship. A village of ten households yet has loyalty and faith. Letting the lord fall into evil, is what the Chūnqiū condemned. Now Liáodōng and Xuántù serve the State Court, winding blue-green and trailing purple,^[This references the blue-green and purple ribbons of office.] numbered in the thousands and hundreds, wearing handscarf and hanging tassels,^[This refers to the headscarfs and hat tassels worn in official government uniforms.] all girdling seal and ribbon, but always without advice of correction and good counsel. When toirtoise shell and jade are destroyed in their cases, tiger and rhinocerous escape their cages, whose fault is it?^[This is an allusion to the Lúnyǔ 16.1. The lower level officials of Liáodōng are being held responsibile for not working to prevent Gōngsūn Yuān's rebellion against Wèi.] The State Court is for you gentlemen ashamed of this! In the past Hú Tū had a saying: "A father that teaches his son to be double-minded, how can he serve lord? Having registered name and entrusted self, double-mindedness then is criminal."^[Hú Tū was a Spring and Autumn era official of Jìn state.] Now yet you flatter and comply with evil schemes, submit to and follow treacherous delusion, how can it only be the teachings of fathers and elder brohters being unclear and the actions of sons and younger brothers being accustomed to wrong and nothing more? If sprouting weeds harm farm the fields, wind spreads the raging fire, the crops and weeds are both burned,^[The term translated as "crops and weeds" is Zhī Ài. Zhī is a name used for various felicitous plants, Ài for artemisia or mugwort. In this context they are used as stand-ins for desirable cultivated plants and undesirable weeds in general.] how can one clearly distinguish them? Moreover also this situation is assuredly easy to see, not reaching to reflecting on antiquity's successes and failures recorded in books and commentaries. The Jiāng's south and Sea's north have a separation of of ten thousand lǐ, Liáodōng's lord and ministers without worry of alarm, seeking profit then righteousness is not considered profitable, seeking nobility then righteous is not considered noble, this is to weary of residing in calm and happiness, to seek the disaster of danger and destruction, to despise the integrity of loyalty and fidelity, to value the reputation for betrayal and rebellion. Even the chieftains of the Mán and Mò yet know to love courtesy. To like this serve others, also would make it difficult to show one's face. Moreover also Sù Shū was without crime, forced to be envoy to enter Wú, serving an unrighteous mission, first with his family bid farewell, shedding tears and going. Reaching to the day of [Zhōu] Hè's death, capsizing multitudes at Chéng mountain,^[Chéng mountain is a mountain at the eastern tip of the Shāndōng peninsula, where Tián Yù intercepted and ambushed Zhōu Hé's fleet as it was returning from Liádōng.] although [Sù] Shū escaped death, his soul left his body.^[Probably this refers to some form of severe mental trauma from the experience.] Why was he forced then to reach to this? Now the loyal ministers and ardent officers are all enraged by Liáodōng's vacillation and treachery, all wish to ride rafts and sail the sea, resolved to unleash their intentions. We are father and mother to Heaven's Under,^[The term for We here is Zhèn, a first person pronoun reserved for the Emperor. The religious and metaphyiscal role of the Emperor is to be an intermediary between humanity and Heaven, that is to be a son of Heaven and parent to humanity.] and additionally consider that Heaven's Under is newly settled,^[This probably refers to Wèi's recent repulsing of a massive joint Shǔ-Wú offensive in 234.] do not wish to toil and mobilize shields and spears, distantly cross great streams, the costs and labors like that, and also lament that the border frontier's remaining numerous people, misled into error like this, and therefore sent Cadet Centrals Wèi Shèn, Shào Mào and others ahead of time to present Edict to show my intentions. If the legs and arms loyal and good are able to prove integrity and establish faith to assist the time's lord, turn from evil to join the correct to establish a great achievement, in fortunes none would be greater. Perhaps you fear and suspect yourself as already being seen as contaminated and defiled by evil rebellion, do not dare to speak out, forever burdened with this regret. Thus for all that with the rebel envoys had exchanges and communications, pardon and exempt them all, to with them start anew."
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　吳書載淵表權曰：「臣伏惟遭天地反易，遇無妄之運；王路未夷，傾側擾攘。自先人以來，歷事漢、魏，階緣際會，為國效節，繼世享任，得守藩表，猶知符命未有攸歸。每感厚恩，頻辱顯使，退念人臣交不越境，是以固守所執，拒違前使。雖義無二信，敢忘大恩！陛下鎮撫，長存小國，前後裴校尉、葛都尉等到，奉被敕誡，聖旨彌密，重紈累素，幽明備著，所以申示之事，言提其耳。臣晝則謳吟，宵則發夢，終身誦之，志不知足。季末凶荒，乾坤否塞，兵革未戢，人民蕩析。仰此天命將有眷顧，私從一隅永瞻雲日。今魏家不能採錄忠善，褒功臣之後，乃令讒訛得行其志，聽幽州刺史、東萊太守誑誤之言，猥興州兵，圖害臣郡。臣不負魏，而魏絕之。蓋聞人臣有去就之分；田饒適齊，樂毅走趙，以不得事主，故保有道之君；陳平、耿況，亦睹時變，卒歸於漢，勒名帝籍。伏惟陛下德不再出，時不世遇，是以慺慺懷慕自納，望遠視險，有如近易。誠願神謨蚤定洪業，奮六師之勢，收河、洛之地，為聖代宗。天下幸甚！」魏略曰：國家知淵兩端，而恐遼東吏民為淵所誤。故公文下遼東，因赦之曰：「告遼東、玄菟將校吏民：逆賊孫權遭遇亂階，因其先人劫略州郡，遂成群凶，自擅江表，含垢藏疾。冀其可化，故割地王權，使南面稱孤，位以上將，禮以九命。權親叉手，北向稽顙。假人臣之寵，受人臣之榮，未有如權者也。狼子野心，告令難移，卒歸反覆，背恩叛主，滔天逆神，乃敢僭號。恃江湖之險阻，王誅未加。比年已來，復遠遣船，越渡大海，多持貨物，誑誘邊民。邊民無知，與之交關。長吏以下，莫肯禁止。至使周賀浮舟百艘，沈滯津岸，貿遷有無。既不疑拒，齎以名馬，又使宿舒隨賀通好。十室之邑，猶有忠信，陷君於惡，春秋所書也。今遼東、玄菟奉事國朝，紆青拖紫，以千百為數，戴纚垂纓，咸佩印綬，曾無匡正納善之言。龜玉毀于匵，虎兕出于匣，是誰之過歟？國朝為子大夫羞之！昔狐突有言：『父教子貳，何以事君？策名委質，貳乃辟也。』今乃阿順邪謀，脅從姦惑，豈獨父兄之教不詳，子弟之舉習非而已哉！若苗穢害田，隨風烈火，芝艾俱焚，安能白別乎？且又此事固然易見，不及鑒古成敗，書傳所載也。江南海北有萬里之限，遼東君臣無怵惕之患，利則義所不利，貴則義所不貴，此為厭安樂之居，求危亡之禍，賤忠貞之節，重背叛之名。蠻、貊之長，猶知愛禮，以此事人，亦難為顏！且又宿舒無罪，擠使入吳，奉不義之使，始與家訣，涕泣而行。及至賀死之日，覆眾成山，舒雖脫死，魂魄離身。何所逼迫，乃至於此！今忠臣烈將，咸忿遼東反覆攜貳，皆欲乘桴浮海，期於肆意。朕為天下父母，加念天下新定，既不欲勞動干戈，遠涉大川，費役如彼，又悼邊陲遺餘黎民，迷誤如此，故遣郎中衛慎、邵瑁等且先奉詔示意。若股肱忠良，能效節立信以輔時君，反邪就正以建大功，福莫大焉。儻恐自嫌已為惡逆所見染汙，不敢倡言，永懷伊戚。其諸與賊使交通，皆赦除之，與之更始。」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-31" id="annotation-31">[31]</a> Wèi lüè records [Gōngsūn] Yuān's memorial stating: "Your Servant formerly sent Colonel Sù Shū and Cadet Centrals Director Sūn Zōng with sweet words and generous gifts, to entice the Wú rebels. By good fortune relying on Heaven's Way blessing and assisting Great Wèi, it cause this rebel caitiff to be blind and deluded, go against his crowd of subordinates, not follow the remonstrations of the multitudes,^[Sūn Quán's minsiters had overwhelmingly opposed his intention to send a large delegation with high ranking envoys and gifts and treasures to title Gōngsūn Yuān as King of Yān.] accept and believe Your Servant's words, distantly send ships and envoys, many officers and soldiers, coming to deliver enfeoffment and appointment. What Your Servant has done, was obtain my original intention, though worrying of guilt and offense, privately I feel extremely fortunate. The rebel multitudes were originally claimed as ten thousand men, [Sù] Shū and [Sūn] Zōng spied and investigated, it could be seven to eight thousand men, arriving at Tàjīn.^[Tàjīn or Tà crossing was probably a ford in Tàishì county in Liáodōng.] The false envoys Zhāng Mí and Xǔ Yàn with Central Cadet General Wàn Tài and Colonel Péi Qián led clerks and soldiers of over four hundred men, presenting written letter and mandated dress and assorted objects, down to arrive at Your Servant's prefecture. [Wàn] Tài and [Péi] Qián separately presented and delivered the gifted goods, wishing to take advantage to sell horses. Army officers Hè Dá and Yú Zī managed the remaining multitudes at the where the ships were. Your Servant originally wished to wait for the cooling season and then capture [Zhāng] Mí and the rest, but [Zhāng] Mí and the rest's men and soldiers were numerous and many, saw that Your Servant did not immediately accept the Wú mandates, and their thoughts had suspicions. Fearing they would act first, dangerous changings suddenly appearing, at once I advanced troops to encircle and capture, cut off the heads of [Zhāng] Mí, [Xǔ] Yàn, [Wàn] Tài, [Péi] Qián and the rest. Their clerks and following soldier multitudes were all servicemen squads and petty men, provided to serve east or west, unable to do as they wished, face bound they begged to surrender,^[Face bound (miàn fù) refers to presenting oneself with arms tied behind the back.] I could not bear to execute and kill them, and at once listened and accepted, exiling them to fill the frontier cities. Separately sent officer Hán Qǐ and others to lead and command the Three Armies, galloping to go to Tà. Sent designate Chief Clerk Liǔ Yuǎn to set up courtesies of guests and hosts to entice and invite [Hè] Dá and [Yú] Zī, the Three Armies hiding in ambush to wait for their coming down, and also herded crowds of horses and goods, wishing to exchange and well. [Hè] Dá and [Yú] Zī were suspicious and did not come down, sending various traders and buyers of five to six hundred men down, wishing to trade. [Hán] Qǐ and the rest's metal drums began to thunder, spearpoints and arrows chaotically fired, cut off heads of over three hundred, the wounded and fel into the waters and drowned could be over two hundred men. Those that scattered and fled into the mountains and valleys, that came to submit and surrender, and hide away and starved to death, are not included in these numbers. The captured silver seals, bronze seals, weapons, supplies, cannot be counted. I solemnly send West Department Assistant Gōngsūn Héng to present and escort the rebel [Sūn] Quán's Lent to Your Servant Stave, Seal and Ribbon, tallies and certificates, Nine Bestowments, assorted goods, with [Zhāng] Mí and the rest's false staves, seals and ribbons, and heads." It also said: "Sù Shū, Sūn Zōng formerly arrived at Wú, the rebel [Sūn] Quán asked about Your Servant's family interior small and large, [Sù] Shū and [Sūn] Zōng replied that Your Servant had three sons, [Gōngsūn] Xiū separately was adopted from a deceased younger brother. [Sūn] Quán dared treacherously scheme, and then without authority appointed and mandated. I solemnly seal and send the seal and ribbon, and tallies and certificates. Although Your Servant is without the men of antiquity's custom of washing ears,^[This refers to the story of the recluse Xǔ Yǒu refusing Yáo's offer to abdicate to him and then washing his ears for having heard such a proposal.] I am ashamed to have been applied the rebel [Sūn] Quán's contaminating harm, having enacted Heaven's punishment, yet still I have remaining anger." It also said: "Your Servant's father [Gōngsūn] Kāng in the past killed [Sūn] Quán's envoy, forming a relationship of enmity. Now then by deceit, I sent envoys to entice and lure, causing [Sūn] Quán to overturn his heart, empty his state and exhaust his resources, distantly mandate his upper minsiters, to lavishly confer utmost position, shaking and disturbing the southern lands, preparing exhaustively numerous courtesies. Also [Sūn] Quán treated [Sù] Shū and [Sūn] Zōng with enduring attachment winding and elaborate,^[The term for enduring attachment (qiè kuò) is from the Shì jīng's song Jī Gǔ, interpreted as meaning "deep hardship" that leads to a close relationship through the sharing of the burdens.] lord and ministers above and below were all joyous and exhaustive in passion. But then I cause his four envoys to meet with death, hanging their heads across ten thousand lǐ, servicemen multitudes wandering in exile, slaughtered and killed on the fords and islets, the shame and humiliation distantly spread, pain and disgrace filling the sky. [Sūn] Quán's resentment and hatred will be engraved on his flesh and bones. If Heaven causes his enterprise to decline, causing it to reach to ruin and fall, [Sūn] Quán will inwardly be injured by indignant rage and so die. If his allotted fate is not yet finished, he will spread his venomous stings, and I must fear the long serpent will come to invade and harm. Xú Province's various garrisons and Chéngyáng various prefectures are bordering and close with him, if there are ships and multitudes in later years heading toward the sea gates, and you obtain this news, I beg it be quickly reported to Your Servant, to allow preparations in advance." It also said: "Your Servant's household received grace, truly deep and truly heavy, from since Your Servant succeeded and took over affairs onward, continuously I received honors and favor, distinct and special immeasurably, my duty is to fall and exceed, exhausting strength in devotion to the death. But Your Servant was rash and foolish, intentions and plans confused and blind, did not immediately take the rebels, and by this met with suspicion. The former Reply Memorial's explanation of interests and circumstances, truly was only a wish to wear and exhaust this rebel, causing him to distress and ruin himself, truly I do not dare turn back on accumulated generations of grace, and attached with a caitiff of usurpation and theft. But later men of favoritisms and hatreds, took advantage of the situation to make false accusations, falsely creating particular details, in the end causing the Enlightened Listener to suspect a marketplace tiger,^[This is an allusion to an old story of a ruler doubting a report of a tiger in the marketplace until hearing three people report it, demonstrating that false reports can be believed if enough people say it.] shifting away grace and changing affections, raising and mobilizing your awe-inspiring fury, almost bringing me to drowning, ever burdened with shame. By good fortune relying upon your compassion and grace, yet I was bequeathed three pardons, allowing me to make amends, resolve and eliminate transgressions and blames. If Heaven's authority were distantly applied, and I did not meet with lending of leniency, I would have quickly been crushed and shattered, disgracing my ancestors and ending their sacrifices, what chance would I have to prove myself, and establish this humble achievement? Your Servant is pleased the matter was successful, to be able to explain and prove myself, but grieve of the past situations, reaching to this unforeseen change, lingering in fear jumping and leaping, I do not yet dare be at ease. May Your Majesty esteem the benevolence of the spring sun preserving life, eliminate anger and close the breach, restrain and repress the minute scruples, consider the present to understand the past, examine Your Servant's original heart, and I will forever cherish and revere it, carrying the debt to the Three Springs.^[Three Springs (sān quán) is a term for the underworld after death.]" It also said: "Your Servant was covered in glory and honor, the grace and kindness not yet repaid, but through crimes and faults, I brought upon myself reprimand and fury, my duty should have been to be killed, to be a warning for the multitudes and society. That I violated standards and departed from norms, falsely communicating with Wú, truly was that I myself reflected upon my desperate circumstances, repayment through service not yet established, but was applied with Heaven's authority and supervisory punishment, ever in fear to suddenly be unable to cleanse myself. Therefore I dared be deficient and absent for one year, sent envoy to entice Wú, knowing they would certainly come. [Sūn] Quán's desire for the prefecture had accumulated for years, formerly I was without the answer of a single word of reply, now [Sūn] Quán was able to send envoys, in coming certain to be without suspicions, so that in one action, indeed it was as I had planned, his upper ministers and great multitudes, imposing and abundant, wealth and gifts, overturning the state with utmost position, on arrival met with capture, the wandering exiles and the death over a thousand men, exterminated and severed to never return. This truly injured the spearpoint of crafty rebel, crushed his boastful scheming, clearly shown to Heaven's Under, breaking and ruining his enterprise, sufficient to shame him. Your Servant's earnest desire is to serve the state, although I have extraordinary faults, I also have extraordinary achievements, may Your Majesty pardon the transgressions of overstepping, recognize the slightest hair of good, to allow me to obtain the state's grace, and remain preserved to the end from the beginning."
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔二〕　魏略載淵表曰：「臣前遣校尉宿舒、郎中令孫綜，甘言厚禮，以誘吳賊。幸賴天道福助大魏，使此賊虜暗然迷惑，違戾群下，不從眾諫，承信臣言，遠遣船使，多將士卒，來致封拜。臣之所執，得如本志，雖憂罪釁，私懷幸甚。賊眾本號萬人，舒、綜伺察，可七八千人，到沓津。偽使者張彌、許晏與中郎將萬泰、校尉裴潛將吏兵四百餘人，齎文書命服什物，下到臣郡。泰、潛別齎致遺貨物，欲因市馬。軍將賀達、虞咨領餘眾在船所。臣本欲須涼節乃取彌等，而彌等人兵眾多，見臣不便承受吳命，意有猜疑。懼其先作，變態妄生，即進兵圍取，斬彌、晏、泰、潛等首級。其吏從兵眾，皆士伍小人，給使東西，不得自由，面縛乞降，不忍誅殺，輒聽納受，徙充邊城。別遣將韓起等率將三軍，馳行至沓。使領長史柳遠設賓主禮誘請達、咨，三軍潛伏以待其下，又驅群馬貨物，欲與交市。達、咨懷疑不下，使諸市買者五六百人下，欲交市。起等金鼓始震，鋒矢亂發，斬首三百餘級，被創赴水沒溺者可二百餘人，其散走山谷，來歸降及藏竄飢餓死者，不在數中。得銀印、銅印、兵器、資貨，不可勝數。謹遣西曹掾公孫珩奉送賊權所假臣節、印綬、符策、九錫、什物，及彌等偽節、印綬、首級。」又曰：「宿舒、孫綜前到吳，賊權問臣家內小大，舒、綜對臣有三息，脩別屬亡弟。權敢姦巧，便擅拜命。謹封送印綬、符策。臣雖無昔人洗耳之風，慚為賊權汙損所加，既行天誅，猶有餘忿。」又曰：「臣父康，昔殺權使，結為讎隙。今乃譎欺，遺使誘致，令權傾心，虛國竭祿，遠命上卿，寵授極位，震動南土，備盡禮數。又權待舒、綜，契闊委曲，君臣上下，畢歡竭情。而令四使見殺，梟示萬里，士眾流離，屠戮津渚，慚恥遠布，痛辱彌天。權之怨疾，將刻肌骨。若天衰其業，使至喪隕，權將內傷憤激而死。若期運未訖，將播毒螫，必恐長蛇來為寇害。徐州諸屯及城陽諸郡，與相接近，如有船眾後年向海門，得其消息，乞速告臣，使得備豫。」又曰：「臣門戶受恩，實深實重，自臣承攝即事以來，連被榮寵，殊特無量，分當隕越，竭力致死。而臣狂愚，意計迷闇，不即禽賊，以至見疑。前章表所陳情趣事勢，實但欲罷弊此賊，使困自絕，誠不敢背累世之恩，附僭盜之虜也。而後愛憎之人，緣事加誣，偽生節目，卒令明聽疑於市虎，移恩改愛，興動威怒，幾至沈沒，長為負忝。幸賴慈恩，猶垂三宥，使得補過，解除愆責。如天威遠加，不見假借，早當麋碎，辱先廢祀，何緣自明，建此微功。臣既喜於事捷，得自申展，悲於疇昔，至此變故，餘怖踊躍，未敢便寧。唯陛下既崇春日生全之仁，除忿塞隙，抑弭纖介，推今亮往，察臣本心，長令抱戴，銜分三泉。」又曰：「臣被服光榮，恩情未報，而以罪釁，自招譴怒，分當即戮，為眾社戒。所以越典詭常，偽通於吳，誠自念窮迫，報效未立，而為天威督罰所加，長恐奄忽不得自洗。故敢自闕替廢於一年，遣使誘吳，知其必來，權之求郡，積有年歲，初無倡答一言之應，今權得使，來必不疑，至此一舉，果如所規，上卿大眾，翕赫豐盛，財貨賂遺，傾國極位，到見禽取，流離死亡，千有餘人，滅絕不反。此誠暴猾賊之鋒，摧矜夸之巧，昭示天下，破損其業，足以慚之矣。臣之慺慺念效於國，雖有非常之過，亦有非常之功，願陛下原其踰闕之愆，采其亳毛之善，使得國恩，保全終始矣。」
:::
:::
:::

<a href="#source-32" id="annotation-32">[32]</a> Wèi Míng Chén zòu records Central Manager of the Army Xiàhóu Xiàn's memorial stating: "Gōngsūn Yuān in former years dared violate Royal commands, cut off his calculated tribute, truly engaged in double-dealing. Having relied on rugged terrain, he also relied on Sūn Quán.^[There is a rhetorical flourish here: the terms for "relied on" is shì for the first instance and hù for the second. In other usages shì is used for reliance on a mother and hù for reliance on a father.] Therefore he dared be domineering, reckless beyond the sea. Sù Shū personally saw the rebel [Sūn] Quán's army multitudes and office treasuries, knew they were weak and feel and not enough to depend upon, and therefore he settled on plans to behead the rebel envoys. Also Gāogōulí, Huìmò with [Gōngsūn] Yuān are enemies, both plundering and raiding. Now outside he has lost Wú's assistance, inside as Hú invaders, inside knows the country is able to follow land routes, in the situation he cannot not have an anxious and fearful heart.  Taking advantage of this time, it is appropriate to send an envoy to explain the disasters and fortunes. Serving Chariots Commandant Zōng Hóng, in Wǔ Huángdì's time first served envoy missions, opening and connecting roads. When Wén Huángdì succeeded the throne, wishing to connect envoy missions, he sent [Zōng] Hóng to lead his wife and children to return to his hometown, bestowed with carriages and oxen, fabric of a hundred pǐ. [Zōng] Hóng had received favor, determined to die for the State Court, without any intention to return, begged to keep his wife and children, and personally serve the envoy mission. Gōngsūn Kāng therefore declared himself servant. With [Zōng] Hóng's serving mission achieved the intention, he was bestowed rank as Marquess Within the Passes. [Zōng] Hóng by nature is resolute and intense, devoting heart to the state, morning to night sincere, intent on exhausting himself in service. A capped clan's descendant, from youth enjoyed learning and inquiry, widely educated in books and records, with much he has related and waded, his mouth fast and nimble in discourse, in debate yet out of the ordinary, draws upon canon statements, as if produced from his own bosom, and additionally served in his home prefecture, always to the right of others, by that region's servicemen always respected and admired. If there is to be an envoy sent, I believe we can send [Zōng] Hóng to go. [Zōng] Hóng then is from the old territory, accustomed to the state's manners, in explaining the benefits and harms, his debate is sufficient to move their thinking, understanding is sufficient to observe their affairs, talent is sufficient to enact it, words sufficient to meet with trust. If this plan is followed, even Lì Shēng's subduing of the King of Qí and Lù Jiǎ's persuasion of Wèi Tuó would be without any distant surpassing.^[This is a reference to the persuasion of the King of Qí to surrender to Liú Bāng during the Chǔ-Hàn contention, and of Wèi Tuó to renounce his own formal claim to title as Emperor and instead accept a title as a King under the nominal auhority of the Hàn Emperor.] In wishing to advance on a distant road, it is not appropriate to set aside thoroughbred steeds. When already seriously ill, it is not appropriate to dismiss Biǎn Què.^[Biǎn Què was a famous Warring States era physician.] May you examine my humble advice."
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔三〕　魏名臣奏載中領軍夏侯獻表曰：「公孫淵昔年敢違王命，廢絕計貢者，實挾兩端。既恃阻險，又怙孫權。故敢跋扈，恣睢海外。宿舒親見賊權軍眾府庫，知其弱少不足憑恃，是以決計斬賊之使。又高句麗、濊貊與淵為仇，並為寇鈔。今外失吳援，內有胡寇，心知國家能從陸道，勢不得不懷惶懼之心。因斯之時，宜遣使示以禍福。奉車都尉鬷弘，武皇帝時始奉使命，開通道路。文皇帝即位，欲通使命，遣弘將妻子還歸鄉里，賜其車、牛，絹百匹。弘以受恩，歸死國朝，無有還意，乞留妻子，身奉使命。公孫康遂稱臣妾。以弘奉使稱意，賜爵關內侯。弘性果烈，乃心於國，夙夜拳拳，念自竭效。冠族子孫，少好學問，博通書記，多所關涉，口論速捷，辯而不俗，附依典誥，若出胸臆，加仕本郡，常在人右，彼方士人素所敬服。若當遣使，以為可使弘行。弘乃自舊土，習其國俗，為說利害，辯足以動其意，明足以見其事，才足以行之，辭足以見信。若其計從，雖酈生之降齊王，陸賈之說尉佗，亦無以遠過也。欲進遠路，不宜釋騏驥；將已篤疾，不宜廢扁鵲。願察愚言也。」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}

<a href="#source-33" id="annotation-33">[33]</a> Wú shū states: Wèi sent envoys Fù Róng, Niè Kuí to appoint [Gōngsūn] Yuān as Duke of Lèlàng. [Gōngsūn] Yuān's Calculations Clerk from Luòyáng returned, spoke to [Gōngsūn] Yuān stating: "The envoy is Zuǒ Jùnbó, those sent are all selected for valor and strength, not ordinary men." [Gōngsūn] Yuān because of this was suspicious and afraid. [Fù] Róng and [Niè] Kuí arrived, stationed inside a school building. [Gōngsūn] Yuān in advance had infantry and cavalry encircle them, and then entered to receive the appointment. [Fù] Róng and [Niè] Kuí were greatly afraid, because of this returned to Luò and reported the situation.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔四〕　吳書曰：魏遣使者傅容、聶夔拜淵為樂浪公。淵計吏從洛陽還，語淵曰：「使者左駿伯，使皆擇勇力者，非凡人也。」淵由是疑怖。容、夔至，住學館中。淵先以步騎圍之，乃入受拜。容、夔大怖，由是還洛言狀。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-34" id="annotation-34">[34]</a> Wèi shū states: [Gōngsūn] Yuān knew this change was not only produced by [Guànqiū] Jiǎn, and therefore made preparations. Sent envoy to apologize to Wú, declared himself King of Yān, requested to become an allied state. However he yet ordered his office associates to send up letter to vindicate himself to Wèi stating: "Marshal-in-Chief's Chief Clerk Your Servant Guō Xīn, Advisor to the Army Your Servant Liǔ Pǔ and others of seven hundred eighty nine men say: Respectfully reciving this year's Seventh Moon Jǐmǎo [237 Aug 28] Edict letter, in prostration reading with earnest sincerity, spirit and soul were scattered apart, not knowing where our bodies and lives would be thrown and placed. [We, Guō] Xīn and the rest in prostration examine ourselves, crickets and ants and petty things, capacity unworthy to be employed in our time, happened to encouter something out a thousand years, received and enjoyed the glorious and brilliant virtue of Gōngsūn Yuān's grandfather and father and onward, beneficence soaking through, nourished with glory and splendor, without a cùn or chǐ of achievement, yet accumulated with burdened carriages.^[Burdened carriages (fù chéng) is a reference to the Yì jīng, commonly interpreted as a metaphor for someone incompetent yet given extraordinary wealth.] therefore covered in commendations and rewards, entering name in Heaven's registers, all as lame horses attached to dragon and entrusted to thoroughbred steed, wound in blue-green and trailing purple, flying and soaring on cloud ladders, moved by gratitude and thinking to repay it, to die without choosing the place. We Your Servants have heard that when an enlightened lord above listens to government and selects advice, servants of men below are able to be without hidden opinions, and therefore we take advantage to present complaints, risking offense to report grievances. The prefecture is on the screen borders, entangled and close with the unruly, ordinarily in the past three provinces transferred contributions and paid costs to provide for bestowal of rewards, annual expenditure accumulating to hundred millions, wastefully consuming the central states. However yet they are domineering, devastating the border areas, signal fires seen from one another, feather dispatches following one another, the city gates in daytime closed, the roads without travelers, provincial and prefecture troops and spears, fleeing and scattering and capsized and lost. [Gōngsūn] Yuān's grandfather [Gōngsūn] Dù first came to oversee the prefecture, inheriting and receiving desolation and ruin, opened the light of sun and moon, established strategy of divine warfare, assembled people of a crow gathering, swept ground as his enterprise,^[A crow gathering (wū hé) is a term for a chaotic unorganized group. Swept ground (sǎodì) is a term for expressing a lack of foundations. Together these emphasize that Gōngsūn Dù started up from almost nothing.] his authority shaking and dazzling those of different customs, virtue and beneficence covering the crowds of living. That Liáo's lands are not destroyed, truly was by depending on [Gōngsūn] Dù. Kǒng-zǐ said: 'Without Guǎn Zhòng, I would have loose hair and left lapels.'^[This quote credits Guǎn Zhòng as rescuing civilization, saying that without his contributions, Kǒng-zǐ would be using foreign customs of unbound hair and having lapel on the left, insteaed of tied hair and lapel on the right.] Supposing if we had not encountered [Gōngsūn] Dù, then the prefecture would long ago have become graves and ruins, and the people bound in caitiff courts. The surviving airs and remnant love, will forever endure without decay. When [Gōngsūn] Dù had died, the clerks and people in gratitude and admiration, happily supported his son [Gōngsūn] Kāng, honoring and serving him. [Gōngsūn] Kāng ascended and united the vast threads, able to strengthen the illustrious plans,^[Illustrious plans (huī yóu) is a line from the Shìjīng's Jiǎogōng, referring to excellent and admirable plans.] civil shining and martial intense, striding virtue nad planting benevolence, devoting heart to capital, cautious in reverent respect, assisting the state and pacifying chaos, providing merits numerous and complex, achievements grand and services great, accomplishments recorded in the Royal Archives. [Gōngsūn] Dù and [Gōngsūn] Kāng happened upon the coincidence of Wǔ Huángdì's glorious and brilliance, joined plans to register names, supporting and assisting the Hàn House, humbling self and pleding hostages, lowering themselves and serving Wèi. It was not being small and repressed by the large or submitting out of fear, rather it was admiration and trust in high winds, embracing and looking up to flourishing virtue. Wǔ Huángdì also with open heart welcomed and accepted, treating them without sequencing, achievements whether massive or minute, every time was not forgotten. Also his mandate to them said: 'The lands north of the sea, are assigned to entrust to you, generation to generation your descendants truly will obtain and possess them.' August Heaven and Lordly Earth, truly heard the virtuous sound. Ministers and commoners small and large, have long been downwind, serving in all around, not daring to fail or neglect. [Gōngsūn] Yuān from birth had the qualities of orchid and stone, in youth embodied teachings of friendliness and fraternity, equipped with the civil and equipped with the martial, loyal and kind and moreover upright, the living people admire and look up, none are not filled with love. [Gōngsūn] Yuān gathered the weapons of his grandfather and father, lord overseeing myriad peoples, acted for the state with courtesy, gently influence flowing and enacted, alone saw before seeing, gathered and bound distant regions, the righteousness of diligently serving King, he viewed the rugged as if flat, for generations conveying loyalty and integrity, not failing his name. Sūn Quán admired his righteousness, not thinking ten thousand lǐ as distant, for continuous years sent envoys, wishing to bind him to be his own assistance, and although he met with cutting off and killing, he did not remember old resentments, but continuously went back and forth, seeking to achieve friendship. [Gōngsūn] Yuān held to integrity increasingly firm, was not swayed by profits, his maintaining of will was not merely stone, indeed it was even hard. Yet fearing his red heart was not yet proven and clear, thus he in humble language and generous gifts, enticed and attracted [Sūn] Quán's envoys, cut off heads and presented the trophies,^[Tropy here is guó, originally a term for the ear of an enemy, cut off and presented as proof of killing an enemy.] to show he was without duplicity. Although Wú is distant, the water routes are easy to cross, raising sails then one arrives, without any separation or limits. [Gōngsūn] Yuān did not regard the deepness of the enmity, but remembered to preserve the integrity of a servant of men, severing the friendship of a strong Wú, to clearly show his heart to serve Wèi. Spirits and deities clearly reflect on it, everywhere Heaven all hears of it. Your Majesty commends and praises vast achievements, admires these martial achievements, accordingly bestows glorious mandates, favor second after Qí and Lǔ,^[Qí and Lǔ were the fief states bestowed on Tàigōng and Zhōugōng by the Zhōu dynasty.] below reaching to the accomapanying ministers, everywhere receiving the great fortunes. Truly with the grave of Heaven's cover, it should have lasted to the end from the beginning, allowing him to exhaust legs and arms, foreover maintain salary and position, but unexpectedly one morning, unreasonably it was cruelly ruined. Considering the generosity of the nurture, remembering the accmuluated services, grieving the thoughts did not materialize, pained to be met with abandonment, the entire state called aloud, beating breast and weeping blood. Those that the Three Armies attack are the Mán Yí Róng Dí, arrogant and not reverent, thereupon it attracts warfare, it is unheard of for a righteous state to instead receive punishment and suppression. By the Regulations of the Sagely Kings, for the area of the Five Regions,^[Five Regions (wǔ fú) refer to an ancient ideal system of concentric zones around the royal center, with varying political obligations based on distance.] if there are those that do not provide duties, then cultivate by civil virtue, and if again it does not arrive, only afterward campaign and attack. [Gōngsūn] Yuān is careful and cautious, respectful in position, diligently serves his superior, and can be said to have made effort. Utterly loyal and exhaustive in integrity, in return he suffers misfortune and disaster. The composition of Xiǎo Biàn, the rise of Lí Sāo, both were because of this.^[Xiǎo Biàn is a song in the Shìjīng, Lí Sāo a song attributed to Qū Yuán. Both of are songs of wrongful rejection.] Even if the flatterers and evil with deceptive words sound sweet, yet there should be pure examination, to reject and know goodness. Skillful slander resembles the upright, confusing and disordering Sagely Listening, but still one would expect written announcement, to allow understanding of the reason. If truly there is a crime, there should be bequeathing of the three pardons. If he does not change and reform, on account of his achievements reducing punishment, there should be the Eight Discussions.^[Eight Discussions (bā yì) refer to a system of granting special considerations to particular cases.] But a secret army suddenly surprise attacked, the main army abruptly arrived, brandishing spears and rushing ahead, charging and striking Liáo territory. Dogs and horses hate death, all the more for human beings! The clerks and civilians risked death to obstruct and disgrace the Royal Brigades. Although [Gōngsūn] Yuān was unjustly accused, right when facing the danger, yet he trusted in sagely grace, sorrowfully again rushing, hoping it must be a traitor minister forging Regulations to recklessly abuse authority and cruelty, and so spoke with We Your Servants stating: "In Hàn Emperor Ān's Jiànguāng Inaugural Year, Liáodōng Dependent State Commandant Páng Fèn received the Third Moon Yǐwèi [121 Apr 19] Edict letting stating: 'Arrest Yōu Province Inspector Féng Huàn, Xuántù Administrator Yáo Guāng.' Investigating the case, there was no Yǐwèi Edict letter, sent Attendant Censor to Yōu Province to arrest and investigate the traitor minister who forged Regulations. Now is the Inspector perhaps is mistakenly obeying a forged Regulation?" We Your Servants discussed, believing: "The Inspector raising troops, shaking and disturbing Heaven's Under, probably is not a forged Regulation, it certainly is an Edict mandate." [Gōngsūn] Yuān then looked down and looked up and sighed, himself pained that he was without crime. Deeply pondering that the land is what nurtures the people, privately admiring Gǔ-gōng leaned on staff to go to Qí,^[This refers to Gǔ-gōng choosing to lead his people to a new land at Qí rather than fight a war. Gǔ-gōng was an ancestor of the ruling house of the Zhōu dynasty.] thus he wished to throw away cap and undo sash, and depart into the woods and foothills. We Your Servants restrained him, swearing to the death, to garrison and defend the office gates, and not allow what he proposed. But the seven camps of Tiger Servicemen, five departments of Mán Yí,^[Tiger Servicemen refers to elite soldiers, said to be as ferocious as tigers. Mán and Yí refer to southern and eastern foreign peoples.] each having their own supplies, had not planned to be alike in heart, exerted arms and greatly shouted, pushing open the gates and rushing out, the nearby suburb farmers released their hoes and spades, cut firewood to make clubs, turned tables into shields, to rush and gallop to face the troubles, an army on the road formed, even treading boiling water and fire, dying without regard for life. Although [Gōngsūn] Yuān met with abandonment, his resentment did not become rage, repeatedly he sent orders to the army, to not transgress and offend, reaching to hand-written letters of announcements, earnest and sorrowful in utmost sincerity. But the clerks and servicemen were fierce and courageous, and could not be disbanded, determined to devote lives, throw into death without regret. [Gōngsūn] Yuān feared the clerks and servicemen would not follow instructions and orders, and so personally galloped, personally going to resolve it, and only barely then stopped them. The kindness of a single meal, a common man would die for, all the more for [Gōngsūn] Yuān's accmuluated generations of faith and bonds with the Hundred Surnames, grace proven in the people's hearts. From since the Former Emperor first rose, reaching to Your Majesty, the glory on [Gōngsūn] Yuān accumulated through generations, abundant achievements and exemplary virtue, registered name commended and praised, discussed clearly in Court and Temple. From since they could wear clothes and put on shoes, they recited and sang the brilliant records, to fill their mouths. To bury and yet dig up is what the ancient people found shameful.^[This refers to a folk story of a racoon failing to accomplish anything due to digging back up what he previously buried.] Xiǎobái and Chóng'ěr were vassal lords of a declining age,^[Xiǎobái and Chóng'ěr were the celebrated hegemons Duke Huán of Qí and Duke Wén of Jìn.] yet admired proven faith, to expand the hegemon's enterprise. The Shī praises King Wén establishing faith with myriad countries, the Lúnyǔ praises Zhòngní leaving food to maintain faith. Faith as a virtue assuredly is very great. Now Wú and Shǔ each have Emperors, legs of a tripod standing, Heaven's Under is shaken and disturbed, not yet united, We Your Servants always for Your Majesty fear these dangerous hearts. [Gōngsūn] Yuān occupies the firmness of metal cities, wields harmonious people, the state prosperous and troops strong, and capable of rampaging. Registering name and entrusting hostages, maintaining to death the good Way, loyalty utmost and righteousness exhaustive, a model for the Nine Provinces. Right now the two enemies watch for openings, it is still unknown who will settle it, to not be warned of this, and instead for [Gōngsūn] Yuān to be harmed, is eating the soft and spitting out the hard, not the Way of a King. Although We Your Servants are lowly, truly we are humbly ashamed of it. If there is no Heaven, Your Servant's one prefecture's good or bad fortune cannot yet be known. If it is said there is a Heaven, then also what would be feared? We Your Servants have heard that in serving a house, in two generations then treat them as master, in three generations then treat them as lord. We Your Servants were born in desolate frontier lands, came out through a jade tablet hole, without great assistance from Wèi, for generations served the Gōngsūn clan, repaying the lives they bestowed is in exerting to the death. In the past Kuǎi Tōng spoke directly, Hàn Zǔ pardoned him from execution. Zhèng Zhān spoke of compliance, Jìn Wén forgave him from death. We Your Servants are obstinate and foolish, do not understand great integrity, but hold to one matter, exposing our liver and guts, words offending dragon scales, the crime deserving ten thousand deaths. May Your Majesty restore and esteem succor and nurture, understand this appeal, to allow your estranged and distant Servants to forever have protection and preservation."
:::

〔五〕　魏書曰：淵知此變非獨出儉，遂為備。遣使謝吳，自稱燕王，求為與國。然猶令官屬上書自直于魏曰：「大司馬長史臣郭昕、參軍臣柳浦等七百八十九人言：奉被今年七月己卯詔書，伏讀懇切，精魄散越，不知身命所當投措！昕等伏自惟省，螻蟻小醜，器非時用，遭值千載，被受公孫淵祖考以來光明之德，惠澤沾渥，滋潤榮華，無寸尺之功，有負乘之累；遂蒙褒獎，登名天府，並以駑蹇附龍託驥，紆青拖紫，飛騰雲梯，感恩惟報，死不擇地。臣等聞明君在上，聽政采言，人臣在下，得無隱情，是以因緣訴讓，冒犯愬冤。郡在藩表，密邇不羈，平昔三州，轉輸費調，以供賞賜，歲用累億，虛耗中國。然猶跋扈，虔劉邊陲，烽火相望，羽檄相逮，城門晝閉，路無行人，州郡兵戈，奔散覆沒。淵祖父度初來臨郡，承受荒殘，開日月之光，建神武之略，聚烏合之民，掃地為業，威震燿于殊俗，德澤被于群生。遼土之不壞，實度是賴。孔子曰：『微管仲，吾其被髮左衽。』向不遭度，則郡早為丘墟，而民係於虜廷矣。遺風餘愛，永存不朽。度既薨殂，吏民感慕，欣戴子康，尊而奉之。康踐統洪緒，克壯徽猷，文昭武烈，邁德種仁；乃心京輦，翼翼虔恭，佐國平亂，效績紛紜，功隆事大，勳藏王府。度、康當值武皇帝休明之會，合策名之計，夾輔漢室，降身委質，卑己事魏。匪處小厭大，畏而服焉，乃慕託高風，懷仰盛懿也。武皇帝亦虛心接納，待以不次，功無巨細，每不見忘。又命之曰：『海北土地，割以付君，世世子孫，實得有之。』皇天后土，實聞德音。臣庶小大，豫在下風，奉以周旋，不敢失墜。淵生有蘭石之姿，少含愷悌之訓，允文允武，忠惠且直；生民欽仰，莫弗懷愛。淵纂戎祖考，君臨萬民，為國以禮，淑化流行，獨見先睹，羅結遐方，勤王之義，視險如夷，世載忠亮，不隕厥名。孫權慕義，不遠萬里，連年遣使，欲自結援，雖見絕殺，不念舊怨，纖纖往來，求成恩好。淵執節彌固，不為利迴，守志匪石，確乎彌堅。猶懼丹心未見保明，乃卑辭厚幣，誘致權使，梟截獻馘，以示無二。吳雖在遠，水道通利，舉帆便至，無所隔限。淵不顧敵讎之深，念存人臣之節，絕彊吳之歡，昭事魏之心，靈祇明鑒，普天咸聞。陛下嘉美洪烈，懿茲武功，誕錫休命，寵亞齊、魯，下及陪臣，普受介福。誠以天覆之恩，當卒終始，得竭股肱，永保祿位，不虞一旦，橫被殘酷。惟育養之厚，念積累之效，悲思不遂，痛切見棄，舉國號咷，拊膺泣血。夫三軍所伐，蠻夷戎狄，驕逸不虔，於是致武，不聞義國反受誅討。蓋聖王之制，五服之域，有不供職，則脩文德，而又不至，然後征伐。淵小心翼翼，恪恭于位，勤事奉上，可謂勉矣。盡忠竭節，還被患禍。小弁之作，離騷之興，皆由此也。就或佞邪，盜言孔甘，猶當清覽，憎而知善；讒巧似直，惑亂聖聽，尚望文告，使知所由。若信有罪，當垂三宥；若不改寤，計功減降，當在八議。而潛軍伺襲，大兵奄至，舞戈長驅，衝擊遼土。犬馬惡死，況於人類！吏民昧死，挫辱王師。淵雖冤枉，方臨危殆，猶恃聖恩，悵然重奔，冀必姦臣矯制，妄肆威虐，乃謂臣等曰：『漢安帝建光元年，遼東屬國都尉龐奮，受三月乙未詔書，曰收幽州刺史馮煥、玄菟太守姚光。推案無乙未詔書，遣侍御史幽州（牧）〔收〕考姦臣矯制者。今刺史或儻謬承矯制乎？』臣等議：以為刺史興兵，搖動天下，殆非矯制，必是詔命。淵乃俛仰歎息，自傷無罪。深惟土地所以養人，竊慕古公杖策之岐，乃欲投冠釋紱，逝歸林麓。臣等維持，誓之以死，屯守府門，不聽所執。而七營虎士，五部蠻夷，各懷素飽，不謀同心，奮臂大呼，排門遁出。近郊農民，釋其耨鎛，伐薪制梃，改案為櫓，奔馳赴難，軍旅行成，雖蹈湯火，死不顧生。淵雖見孤棄，怨而不怒，比遣敕軍，勿得干犯，及手書告語，懇惻至誠。而吏士凶悍，不可解散，期於畢命，投死無悔。淵懼吏士不從教令，乃躬馳騖，自往化解，僅乃止之。一飯之惠，匹夫所死，況淵累葉信結百姓，恩著民心。自先帝初興，爰暨陛下，榮淵累葉，豐功懿德，策名褒揚，辯著廊廟，勝衣舉履，誦詠明文，以為口實。埋而掘之，古人所恥。小白、重耳，衰世諸侯，猶慕著信，以隆霸業。詩美文王作孚萬邦，論語稱仲尼去食存信；信之為德，固亦大矣。今吳、蜀共帝，鼎足而居，天下搖蕩，無所統一，臣等每為陛下懼此危心。淵據金城之固，仗和睦之民，國殷兵彊，可以橫行。策名委質，守死善道，忠至義盡，為九州表。方今二敵闚〈門俞〉，未知孰定，是之不戒，而淵是害。茹柔吐剛，非王者之道也。臣等雖鄙，誠竊恥之。若無天乎，臣一郡吉凶，尚未可知；若云有天，亦何懼焉！臣等聞仕於家者，二世則主之，三世則君之。臣等生於荒裔之土，出於圭竇之中，無大援於魏，世隸於公孫氏，報生與賜，在於死力。昔蒯通言直，漢祖赦其誅；鄭詹辭順，晉文原其死。臣等頑愚，不達大節，苟執一介，披露肝膽，言逆龍鱗，罪當萬死。惟陛下恢崇撫育，亮其控告，使疏遠之臣，永有保持。」

<a href="#source-35" id="annotation-35">[35]</a> Hàn Jìn Chūnqiū states: Gōngsūn Yuān established himself, declaring Shàohàn Inaugural Year.^[The Year Name Shào Hàn can be interpreted as "succeeding Hàn," implicity declaring Wèi as illegitimate and presenting his Yān state as the true successor of Hàn.] Hearing the Wèi men was about to suppress, he again declared himself servant to Wú, begging for troops to attack north to rescue him. The Wú men wished to kill his envoys, Yáng Chén said: "It cannot be. It is to indulge in an ordinary fellow's anger and abandon the planning of Hegemons and Kings. It is not as good as taking advantage to be generous to them, send surprise troops to secretly go to intercept the successes. If Wèi attacks [Gōngsūn] Yuān and is not successful, but our army comes from afar, it is our grace bonding with distant Yí, righteousness covering ten thousand lǐ. If the troops are continuously not resolved, head and tail separated apart, then we will capture their nearby prefectures, charging to raid and then return, also sufficient to deliver the punishments of Heaven, and avenge and clear the former matter." [Sūn] Quán said: "Excellent." Thus organized troops to greatly set out. He spoke with [Gōngsūn] Yuān's envoy stating: "Please await later news, there will be following letters. I certainly will with my younger brother share in glory and sorrow, together in survival or destruction, even if I fall in the central plains, I would be willing in heart." He also said: "Where Sīmǎ Yì advances none withstands, I am extremely worried for my younger brother."

〔六〕　漢晉春秋曰：公孫淵自立，稱紹漢元年。聞魏人將討，復稱臣於吳，乞兵北伐以自救。吳人欲戮其使，羊茞曰：「不可，是肆匹夫之怒而捐霸王之計也。不如因而厚之，遣奇兵潛往以要其成。若魏伐淵不克，而我軍遠赴，是恩結遐夷，義蓋萬里，若兵連不解，首尾離隔，則我虜其傍郡，驅略而歸，亦足以致天之罰，報雪曩事矣。」權曰：「善」。乃勒兵大出。謂淵使曰：「請俟後問，當從簡書，必與弟同休戚，共存亡，雖隕于中原，吾所甘心也。」又曰：「司馬懿所向無前，深為弟憂也。」
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Previously, [Gōngsūn] Yuān's house repeatedly had strangeness. A dog in cap and headcloth and purple-read robe went up a room, while cooking there was a small child steamed to death inside a cauldron. In Xiāngpíng's north market appeared flesh, length and circumference each several chǐ, having head and eyes and mouth and snout, without hands and feat but yet moving and swaying. Divination said: "It has form but is incomplete, has body but no voice, this is the state's destruction." Beginning from [Gōngsūn] Dù in Zhōngpíng Sixth Year occupying Liáodōng reaching to [Gōngsūn] Yuān as the third generation was altogether fifty years and then destruction. <a href="#annotation-36" id="source-36">[36]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
初，淵家數有怪，犬冠幘絳衣上屋，炊有小兒蒸死甑中。襄平北巿生肉，長圍各數尺，有頭目口喙，無手足而動搖。占曰：「有形不成，有體無聲，其國滅亡。」始度以中平六年據遼東，至淵三世，凡五十年而滅。〔一〕

<a href="#source-36" id="annotation-36">[36]</a> Wèi lüè states: Formerly [Gōngsūn] Yuān's elder brother [Gōngsūn] Huǎng was [Gōngsūn] Gōng's hostage son at Luò, heard that [Gōngsūn] Yuān had seized away [Gōngsūn] Gōng's position, said [Gōngsūn] Yuān in the end could not be guaranteed, and repeatedly himself memorialized news, wishing to have the country suppress [Gōngsūn] Yuān. The Emperor because [Gōngsūn] Yuān already held power therefore accomodated and succored him. Reaching to [Gōngsūn] Yuān's rebellion, therefore by the state's laws arrested [Gōngsūn] Huǎng. Although [Gōngsūn] Huǎng had previously spoken out and hoped to not be connected, however inwardly because they were bone and flesh, he knew when [Gōngsūn] Yuān was destroyed then he himself would follow. When [Gōngsūn] Yuān's head arrived, [Gōngsūn] Huǎng himself judged he would certainly die, with his children facing each other and weeping. At the time the Superior also wished to spare him, but the relevant managers believed it not permissible, therefore killed him.

〔一〕　魏略曰：始淵兄晃為恭任子，在洛，聞淵劫奪恭位，謂淵終不可保，數自表聞，欲令國家討淵。帝以淵已秉權，故因而撫之。及淵叛，遂以國法繫晃。晃雖有前言，冀不坐，然內以骨肉，知淵破則己從及。淵首到，晃自審必死，與其子相對啼哭。時上亦欲活之，而有司以為不可，遂殺之。

## Zhāng Yàn {.unnumbered #zhangyan}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Zhāng Yàn was a Chángshān Zhēndìng man, originally surnamed Chǔ. When the Huángjīn rose up, [Chǔ] Yàn united and assembled youths into a crowd of robbers, among the mountains and marshes turning and attacking, returning to Zhēndìng, the multitudes over ten thousand people. Bólíng's Zhāng Niújiǎo^[Niújiǎo "Ox Horn" is probably a sobriquet rather than a personal name.] also raised multitudes, declared himself Commanding Troops Following Official, with [Chǔ] Yàn uniting. [Chǔ] Yàn nominated [Zhāng] Niújiǎo as the commander, together they attacked Yíngtáo.^[Yíngtǎo county was in Jùlù prefecture.] [Zhāng] Niújiǎo was by a stray arrow hit, was wounded and about to die, ordered the multitudes to serve [Chǔ] Yàn, the announcement stating: "You must take Yàn as commander." Niújiǎo died, the multitudes served Yàn, therefore he changed his surname to Zhāng. [Zhāng] Yàn was fierce and bold, nimble and fast surpassing other men, therefore inside the army they called him Fēiyàn.^[Fēiyàn "Flying Swallow" is a sobriquet incorporating Zhāng Yàn's personal name, which can mean "swallow."] From then afterward the men and multitudes gradually spread, Chángshān's, Zhào prefecture's, Zhōngshān's, Shàngdǎng's, Hénèi's various mountain valleys were all interconnected, the smaller commanders Sūn Qīng and Wáng Dāng and others each with their division multitudes followed [Zhāng] Yàn, the multitudes reached a million, called as Hēishān.^[Hēishān "Black Mountain" was the name of the bandit confederation.] Emperor Líng was unable to campaign against them, north of the Hé the various prefectures suffered the harm. [Zhāng] Yàn sent someone to the capital city to ask to surrender, appointed [Zhāng] Yàn as Pacifying Troubles Central Cadet General. <a href="#annotation-37" id="source-37">[37]</a> From then afterward, Dǒng Zhuó moved Heaven's Son to Cháng'ān, Under Heaven troops repeatedly rose, [Zhāng] Yàn therefore with his multitudes joined together with towering heroes. Yuán Shào with Gōngsūn Zàn contested Jì Province, [Zhāng] Yàn sent his officer Dù Zhǎng and others to assist [Gōngsūn] Zàn, with [Yuán] Shào battled, was by [Yuán] Shào defeated, the men and multitudes gradually scattered. When Tàizǔ was about to settle Jì Province, [Zhāng] Yàn sent envoy to request to assist the Royal Brigades, appointed Pacifying North General. He led his multitudes to visit Yè, enfeoffed Marquess of Ānguó precinct, estate of five hundred households. [Zhāng] Yàn died, his son [Zhāng] Fāng succeeded. [Zhāng] Fāng died, his son [Zhāng] Róng succeeded. <a href="#annotation-38" id="source-38">[38]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
張燕，常山真定人也，本姓褚。黃巾起，燕合聚少年為群盜，在山澤閒轉攻，還真定，眾萬餘人。博陵張牛角亦起眾，自號將兵從事，與燕合。燕推牛角為帥，俱攻廮陶。牛角為飛矢所中。被創且死，令眾奉燕，告曰：「必以燕為帥。」牛角死，眾奉燕，故改姓張。燕剽捍捷速過人，故軍中號曰飛燕。其後人眾寢廣，常山、趙郡、中山、上黨、河內諸山谷皆相通，其小帥孫輕、王當等，各以部眾從燕，眾至百萬，號曰黑山。靈帝不能征，河北諸郡被其害。燕遣人至京都乞降，拜燕平難中郎將。〔一〕是後，董卓遷天子於長安，天下兵數起，燕遂以其眾與豪傑相結。袁紹與公孫瓚爭冀州，燕遣將杜長等助瓚，與紹戰，為紹所敗，人眾稍散，太祖將定冀州，燕遣使求佐王師，拜平北將軍；率眾詣鄴，封安國亭侯，邑五百戶。燕薨，子方嗣。方薨，子融嗣。〔二〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-37" id="annotation-37">[37]</a> Jiǔzhōu Chūnqiū states: In Zhāng Jué's rebellion, Hēishān, Báibō, Huánglóng, Zuǒ Jiào, Niújiǎo, Wǔlù, Dīgēn, Kǔqiú, Liú Shí, Píng Hàn, Dà Hóng, Sīlì, Yuánchéng, Luóshì, Léigōng, Fúyún, Fēiyàn, Bái Jué, Yáng Fèng, Yú Dú and others each raised troops, the large twenty to thirty thousand, the small not less than several thousand. Emperor Líng was unable to suppress them, and so sent envoys to appoint Yáng Fèng as Black Mountain Colonel, managing the various mountain bandits, able to nominate Filial-Incorruptible and Calculation Clerks. Later they then all the more spread, and could not be further counted.

Diǎnlüè states: The Hēishān and Huángjīn various commanders originally were not capped and canopied, and themselves gave each other sobriquets and appellations,^[Capped and canopied (guān gài) refer to the gentry classes, who wore caps and rode canopied carriages, and had appellations. The bandit leaders were not of the gentry classes, but began to use sobriquets, perhaps in something of a crude imitation of the gentry appellations.] calling the one riding the white horse as Zhāng Báiqí,^[Báiqí is "White Rider."] calling the light and nimble one as Zhāng Fēiyàn^[Fēiyàn is "Flying Swallow." This was Zhāng Yàn.] calling the one with loud voice as Zhāng Léigōng,^[Léigōng can be understood as "Duke of Thunder" or "Lord of Thunder."] the one with abundant beard then declared himself Yú Dīgēn,^[Dī can refer to a billy goat or ram, gēn means "root." The sobriquet refers to having a beard like a billy goat.] the one with big eyes declared himself Lǐ Dàmù.^[Dàmù is "Big Eyes."]

Zhāng Fán's Hàn jì says: Also there was Zuǒ Jiào,^[Jiào can be "fetters" or "shackles." The character can also be xiào "school" or xiào "colonel" though these readings seem less likely for a bandit sobriquet.] Guō Dàxián,^[Dàxián can be interpreted as "Great Worthy."] Zuǒ Zīzhàngbā^[Zīzhàngbā might be intended to mean "mustache eight zhàng (long)." During Later Hàn, eight zhàng would be about 18.5 meters, or a litle over 60 feet. Obviously the measurement was not literal.] three divisions.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　九州春秋曰：張角之反也，黑山、白波、黃龍、左校、牛角、五鹿、羝根、苦蝤、劉石、平漢、大洪、司隸、緣城、羅市、雷公、浮雲、飛燕、白爵、楊鳳、于毒等各起兵，大者二三萬，小者不減數千。靈帝不能討，乃遣使拜楊鳳為黑山校尉，領諸山賊，得舉孝廉計吏。後遂彌漫，不可復數。典略曰：黑山、黃巾諸帥，本非冠蓋，自相號字，謂騎白馬者為張白騎，謂輕捷者為張飛燕，謂聲大者為張雷公，其饒鬚者則自稱于羝根，其眼大者自稱李大目。張璠漢紀云：又有左校、郭大賢、左髭丈八三部也。
:::
:::
:::

<a href="#source-38" id="annotation-38">[38]</a> Lú Jī's Jìn Huìdì Qǐjū zhù states: Below the Gates Communicating Affairs Director Scribe Zhāng Lín was [Zhāng] Yàn's great-grandson. [Zhāng] Lín with the King of Zhào [Sīmǎ] Lún made chaos, in not reaching a full year, his position reached Secretariat Writers Director, Guard General, enfeoffed Duke of a prefecture. Soon afterward he was killed by [Sīmǎ] Lún.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔二〕　陸機晉惠帝起居注曰：門下通事令史張林，飛燕之曾孫。林與趙王倫為亂，未及周年，位至尚書令、衛將軍，封郡公。尋為倫所殺。

## Zhāng Xiù {.unnumbered #zhangxiu}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Zhāng Xiù was a Wǔwēi Zǔlì man, Agile Cavalry General [Zhāng] Jì's clan's son.^[A clan's son or cousin's son (zú zǐ) variously referred to the son of a male-line second cousin or son of a male-line third cousin.] Biān Zhāng and Hán Suì made chaos in Liáng Province, Jīnchéng's Qū Shèng surprise attacked and killed the Zǔlì Chief Liú Juàn. [Zhāng] Xiù was a county clerk, watched for an opening and killed [Qū] Shèng, inside the prefecture regarded it righteous. Therefore he recruited and united youths, becoming a towering hero within the city. When Dǒng Zhuó was destroyed, [Zhāng] Jì with Lǐ Jué and the rest struck Lǚ Bù, for [Dǒng] Zhuó taking revenge. The story is in [Dǒng] [Zhuó's biography](06.qmd#dongzhuo). [Zhāng] Xiù accompanied [Zhāng] Jì, for army achievements gradually promoted to reach Establishing Loyalty General, enfeoffed Marquess of Xuānwēi.^[Xuānwēi county was in Wǔwēi prefecture.] [Zhāng] Jì garrisoned Hóngnóng, the soldiers were starving, to the south he attacked Ráng, was hit by a stray arrow and died. [Zhāng] Xiù took over the multitudes, garrisoned Wǎn, with Liú Biǎo joining. Tàizǔ campaigned south, the army stationed the Yù river, [Zhāng] Xiù and the rest led the multitudes to surrender. Tàizǔ accepted as concubine [Zhāng] Jì's wife, [Zhāng] Xiù resented this. Tàizǔ heard of his displeasure, secretly had a plan to kill [Zhāng] Xiù. The plan leaked, [Zhāng] Xiù surprise attacked Tàizǔ, Tàizǔ's army was defeated, two sons lost. [Zhāng] Xiù returned to protect Ráng, <a href="#annotation-39" id="source-39">[39]</a> Tàizǔ for successive years attacked him, not successful. Tàizǔ resisted Yuán Shào at Guāndù, [Zhāng] Xiù followed Jiǎ Xǔ's plan, again with his multitudes surrendered. The story is in [Jiǎ] [Xǔ's biography](10.qmd#jiaxu). [Zhāng] Xiù arrived, Tàizǔ grasped his hand, with him celebrated and feasted, for his son [Cáo] Jūn obtained [Zhāng] Xiù's daughter, appointed Raising Warfare General. In the Guāndù campaign, [Zhāng] Xiù fought hard and had achievements, promoted to Breaking Qiāng General. Accompanied in defeating Yuán Tán at Nánpí, further increased his estate altogether to two thousand households. At the time Heaven's Under's registered population was reduced and depleted, out of ten only one remained, the varioius officers' enfeoffments had never yet had any as many as thousand households, but yet [Zhāng] Xiù's was especially many. Accompanied the campaign against the Wūhuán to Liǔchéng, had not yet arrived, died, posthumous name called Dìng-hóu. <a href="#annotation-40" id="source-40">[40]</a> His son [Zhāng] Quán succeeded, in connection to Wèi Fěng's plot to rebel was executed, state abolished.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
張繡，武威祖厲人，驃騎將軍濟族子也。邊章、韓遂為亂涼州，金城麴勝襲殺祖厲長劉雋。繡為縣吏，閒伺殺勝，郡內義之。遂招合少年，為邑中豪傑。董卓敗，濟與李傕等擊呂布，為卓報仇。語在卓傳。繡隨濟，以軍功稍遷至建忠將軍，封宣威侯。濟屯弘農，士卒飢餓，南攻穰，為流矢所中死。繡領其眾，屯宛，與劉表合。太祖南征，軍淯水，繡等舉眾降。太祖納濟妻，繡恨之。太祖聞其不悅，密有殺繡之計。計漏，繡掩襲太祖。太祖軍敗，二子沒。繡還保穰，〔一〕太祖比年攻之，不克。太祖拒袁紹於官渡，繡從賈詡計，復以眾降。語在詡傳。繡至，太祖執其手，與歡宴，為子均取繡女，拜揚武將軍。官渡之役，繡力戰有功，遷破羌將軍。從破袁譚於南皮，復增邑凡二千戶。是時天下戶口減耗，十裁一在，諸將封未有滿千戶者，而繡特多。從征烏丸于柳城，未至，薨，諡曰定侯。〔二〕子泉嗣，坐與魏諷謀反誅，國除。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-39" id="annotation-39">[39]</a> Fù-zǐ states: [Zhāng] Xiù had an intimate Hú Chē'ér, bravery highest in the army. Tàizǔ favored his valor and vigor, with his own hand giving him gold. [Zhāng] Xiù heard and suspected Tàizǔ wished to use his Left and Right assassinate him, and therefore rebelled.

Wú shū states: [Zhāng] Xiù surrendered, employed Jiǎ Xǔ's plan, requested to relocate his army on a high road, the road went through Tàizǔ's garrison. [Zhāng] Xiù also said: "The carriages are few but heavy, I request to have the soldiers each wear armor." Tàizǔ trusted [Zhāng] Xiù, and all permitted it. [Zhāng] Xiù then readied troops and entered the garrison, surpise attacked Tàizǔ. Tàizǔ was not prepared, and therefore defeated.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　傅子曰：繡有所親胡車兒，勇冠其軍。太祖愛其驍健，手以金與之。繡聞而疑太祖欲因左右刺之，遂反。吳書曰：繡降，（凌統）用賈詡計，乞徙軍就高道，道由太祖屯中。繡又曰：「車少而重，乞得使兵各被甲。」太祖信繡，皆聽之。繡乃嚴兵入屯，掩太祖。太祖不備，故敗。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-40" id="annotation-40">[40]</a> Wèilüè states: The Five Office General [Cáo Pī] repeatedly took advantage to invite him to gatherings, expressed anger stating: "You killed my elder brother, how dare you show your face to others?" [Zhāng] Xiù in his heart could not be at ease with himself, and so killed himself.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔二〕　魏略曰：五官將數因請會，發怒曰：「君殺吾兄，何忍持面視人邪！」繡心不自安，乃自殺。
:::
